While most raccoons are seen as a nuisance, going through people’s garbage and potentially carrying rabies, one masked bandit scurrying through Seattle yards has stolen the hearts of locals.

The mutant-looking raccoon named Jimothy has been all over social media, gaining buzz for his uniquely curved back.

In one video posted on Instagram, Jimothy was seen prancing across a lawn before going up concrete steps.

The woman filming the video can be heard saying, “What am I looking at?”

She said in the post’s caption that she and her partner “were graced with the presence of Jimothy the raccoon with short spine syndrome. Praise Jimothy!!”

‘Jimothy,’ a mutant raccoon with a rare, short-spine condition has take Seattle by storm ( TMZ via Video Elephant )

Short spine syndrome is a rare genetic condition that significantly shortens the spine. Some people may have seen the condition in dogs that have very short necks.

One Reddit user shared a clip of Jimothy on a balcony, squeezing through two bars in the railing.

Fans couldn’t get enough of the critter, with one Reddit user commenting, “I desire a repository of more Jimothy videos and pictures, PLEEEEASE.”

“Petition to make Jimothy the state animal or Seattle mascot,” another wrote.

“Hot Jimothy Summer,” a third wrote, riffing off “Hot Girl Summer.”

The phrase comes from rapper Megan Thee Stallion’s 2019 song “Hot Girl Summer.” At the time, she cleared up what it meant: “Being a Hot Girl is about being unapologetically YOU, having fun, being confident, living YOUR truth , being the life of the party etc.”

Washington’s Fish and Wildlife Department told The Independent it has not received any calls about Jimothy.

The department says it’s common to find Raccoons in the state, often in urban areas with food.

“As long as raccoons are kept out of human homes, not cornered, and not treated as pets, they are not dangerous,” the department writes on its website.

Matty Healy, the frontman of The 1975, has married his model and musician girlfriend Gabbriette Bechtel two years after getting engaged – and just weeks after his ex Taylor Swift’s high-profile wedding to Travis Kelce.

While Swift’s wedding took over New York’s Madison Square Garden on Thanksgiving weekend, Healy, 37, and Bechtel, 28, reportedly said “I do” at Los Angeles’ Castillo del Lago, located underneath the Hollywood sign.

Those in attendance included Charli XCX, who is married to The 1975 drummer George Daniel, as well as actor and model Emily Ratajkowski.

open image in gallery Matty Healy has married Gabbriette Bechtel in Los Angeles ( Getty Images )

Healy, whose band headlined Glastonbury in 2025, is also said to have performed a set with his fellow musicians at the wedding reception. The Independent has contacted Healy and Bechtel for comment.

The 1975 star proposed to gothic fashionista Bechtel with a black diamond ring in June 2024. She debuted the grungy engagement ring in a June 12 post on Instagram, with the caption: “Brat city b****.” The style mogul was seen pouting with black liner smudged under her eyes, as she held her ring finger up for the camera.

Healy’s mother, Denise Welch, confirmed the couple was engaged while speaking on the ITV talk show Loose Women. She admitted Bechtel’s Instagram post came a few weeks after her son’s proposal.

“I have known for a few weeks that Matty got engaged,” Welch said. “They went over to see their friends, Charli and George, in New York and I woke up this morning to the fact they’ve put it on Instagram.”

“Black diamond; he had it made for her,” Welch noted of Bechtel’s engagement ring.

open image in gallery Matty Healy of The 1975 performs on the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury 2025 ( BBC )

According to an interview with Vogue UK, Bechtel wants to have children with Healy – and has already setting some ground rules for the dinner table.

“When I have kids, it’s going to be: dinner every night – no phones – to celebrate the smaller things and recognize people’s happiness,” she told the outlet in July 2024.

Before her relationship with the 1975singer, Bechtel dated Bob Dylan’s grandson, Levi Dylan, in 2020. Elsewhere during her interview with Vogue UK, the gothic fashionista admitted that she’d never truly been in love before.

“I love being in love... When I thought that I was in love before it was just me being a person of service to somebody else,” she told the outlet, adding that her relationship with Healy is true love.

Healy had a brief fling with Swift in 2024 – and even inspired several songs on her record The Tortured Poets Department, including a “diss track” called “The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived”.

News.title: Antonelli wins Belgian Grand Prix to extend championship lead after Russell crashes out
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli saw off a challenge from Charles Leclerc to get back to winning ways at the Belgian Grand Prix on Sunday as his team-mate and title rival George Russell failed to finish.

Antonelli started on pole but lost the lead to Leclerc when a virtual safety car slowdown allowed the Ferrari driver to save time during his pit stop.

Antonelli sped back past Leclerc with 10 laps remaining and cruised from there to his sixth win of the season and first since last month’s Monaco Grand Prix.

Leclerc was second and Max Verstappen was third after briefly taking, then losing, the lead from Antonelli on the opening lap.

The Italian stretched his standings lead after Russell was left stuck in the gravel on the first lap after he was pushed into a spin by Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton.

Antonelli went into the race with a 25-point lead over Russell after recent reliability issues for the Italian cut his advantage. That has now nearly doubled. Antonelli will leave Belgium with a 45-point gap over Hamilton, who moved up to second, and is 50 ahead of Russell.

More to follow...

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

News.title: Hometown hero Tommy Fleetwood facing tough ask to end 57 years of Open hurt
News.content:
Never mind Bryson DeChambeau stomping around in the rough as he improved his lie, for so long this Open Saturday turned into Tommy Fleetwood walking in his Royal Birkdale wonderland as he enhanced the mood of seemingly everyone in attendance.

Alas, the fun could not last and, even though he still has a chance of becoming England’s first Open winner on English soil since 1969, that finish looked costly. Fifty-seven years of hurt and all that...

On five under, Fleetwood is in a tie for ninth, five off the lead held by Sam Burns, the American who, after a 65, is two clear of New Zealander Ryan Fox and South Korean Kim Si-woo. DeChambeau is alongside Swede Ludvig Aberg, in a tie for sixth on six under, after a 69.

He was heckled on the 18th because of the two-shot penalty he received on Friday night for “inadvertently improving his lie” on the fifth. “You’re a cheat, Bryson,” the fan shouted.

It was a sour point that was in no way in keeping with the mood of this Saturday that had been overwhelmingly positive. With Fleetwood as the focus, of course.

The enormous crowd cheered and sang and backed their fellow Merseysider all the way as Fleetwood launched his charge into contention at this Southport links which he would once sneak on as a child. His playing partner, Jon Rahm, was taken aback by the level of support.

“The best way I can explain it, it was so intense that, without meaning any disrespect I’m glad England didn’t win the semi-final [of the World Cup] because I would have been having a heck of a three days with the fans if they had been playing Spain in tomorrow’s final,” Rahm said.

News.title: Sloppy Springboks still strong enough to pulverise Wales
News.content:
If one image summed up South Africa’s complete control, it was in the 12th minute when Wales had a scrum on their own five-metre line. When the Springbok shove came, the Welsh pack went backwards like they were on roller-skates. The poor Welsh front row are going to have to check under their beds for snarling Springboks props for quite a few sleepless nights to come.

Wales’ best period of the game came just after the Springboks’ fourth try when they had three line-outs and took three tap penalties deep inside the South Africa 22. It amounted to absolutely nothing.

You can point fingers at head coach Steve Tandy’s selections and preparation if you wish, but there was little he could have done to change the result. It was only the manner of their hammering, he could have potentially affected.

Wales are not alone in this. Scotland and England may have posed a few more problems but they were still dispatched with ease. South Africa are truly in a league of their own, although New Zealand’s resurgence under Dave Rennie should at least provide a serious level of competition that the British mainland failed to provide.

In truth the best thing that Tandy could do is burn the tapes and hope that this is consigned to the deepest recesses of their collective memory. Tighthead Dillon Lewis especially may need one of those Men in Black memory wipers.

If you squinted hard enough, there were a couple of positives: the maul defence and high-ball contest. They were at least competitive. Aaron Wainwright had the unenviable job of packing down at the back of a retreating Welsh scrum but did a heroic job in the circumstances. Jac Morgan, too, was bravery personified in attacking the breakdown with the ferocity of the Springboks clean-out operation.

But in the infrequent periods when South Africa got on a roll without knocking on, there was precious little Wales could do to stop the green wave. The first try was a case in point. Emanating from a loose kick from Tomos Williams, full-back Aphelele Fassi broke the first line of Wales’ defence and then they kept coming through Cobus Wiese, Damien de Allende before Jasper Wiese accelerated through Morgan’s tackle and over the line.

News.title: Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham
News.content:
United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

Sports.title: World Cup final LIVE: Spain vs Argentina team news and weather latest after England win
Sports.content:
Messi and Yamal will go head-to-head in New Jersey

Reigning World Cup champions Argentina will face the kings of Europe Spain in Sunday's clash in New York to decide who takes home the top prize following England's success over France in the bronze final

Today is the day. Either Spain or Argentina will become champions of the world tonight.

The two top ranked sides on the planet will clash in New Jersey in the World Cup final. Argentina, who beat England in a dramatic semi-final, are aiming to become the first side since Brazil in 1962 to retain their crown.

While Spain can win their second World Cup in 16 years after dominating France in the last four.

Meanwhile, England sealed their best finish at a World Cup for 60 years by beating France 6-4 in a scarcely believable bronze final on Saturday night.

Kick off is at 8pm tonight, but we will have all the build up to the big game, plus all the reaction to England's win, before live updates once we are underway....

Sports.title: Spain vs Argentina kick-off time decision as FIFA respond to World Cup final 'threat'
Sports.content:
Spain vs Argentina kick-off time decision as FIFA respond to World Cup final 'threat'

Spain take on Argentina at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday evening, with thunderstorms threatening FIFA's planned 8pm kick-off time for their showpiece

View Image Sunday's World Cup final will go ahead as planned (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

The 2026 World Cup final will go ahead at its scheduled 8pm kick-off time, despite fears of disruption through thunderstorms. Spain and Argentina are set to get underway at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday evening, as this summer's tournament in North America reaches its climax.

‌



World Football's most prestigious tournament hasn't been without its teething problems due to unpredictable weather, with a number of matches being postponed of delayed for hours as a result of thunder and lightning. As per US law, any lightning within an eight-mile radius puts a pause on play for at least half an hour until the last detected strike.

‌



That was witnessed during France's group stage clash with Iraq last month, with proceedings being halted for almost two hours due to stormy conditions in and around the Lincoln Financial Field. England's round of 16 battle with Mexico at the Estadio Azteca, meanwhile, was also postponed by an hour due to storms.

‌



Argentina players refuse to give Falklands banner back after England World Cup controversy READ MORE :

BBC's Joe Hart in bizarre video before World Cup final with pundit DRENCHED in monsoon weather READ MORE :

Sunday's final encounter between Spain and Argentina was also cast into speculation as a result of forecasted thunderstorms across New Jersey. Smoke drifting south of the border through Canadian wildfires also brought fears that the location of the showpiece could be moved altogether due to diminished air quality.

However, FIFA have now confirmed that no changes will be made to the 8pm kick-off time, nor the venue, as conditions continue to be monitored alongside the National Weather Service. It comes as thunderstorms has already disrupted both finalists' preparations.

Spain were scheduled to hold an outdoor training session on Saturday at the Melanie Lane Training Ground, only for it to be suspended due to lightning moving into the locale. A statement was subsequently issued by the Spanish Football Federation.

‌



It read: "The Spanish national team's training session on the pitches at the Melanie Lane Training Ground in New Jersey has been suspended in accordance with the US storm safety protocol. The players are currently taking part in a warm-up session indoors."

Argentina also had to make changes to their own training session in Morristown, kick-starting their preparations 45 minutes late as a result of the adverse weather. It comes as the European and World Champions go head to head on Sunday evening.

Luis de la Fuente's Spain secured their spot in the final thanks to a 2-0 rout over France on Tuesday, Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro making the difference in that encounter. Argentina, meanwhile, enjoyed a 2-1 win over England on Wednesday, with late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez cancelling out Anthony Gordon's opener.

Article continues below

England and France played out a third-place play-off clash in Miami, Florida, on Saturday evening - in what landed as a formality rather than any sort of prestigious encounter. England ultimately ran out 6-4 winners during that game, thanks to a Bukayo Saka hattrick and additional goals from Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and Jude Bellingham.

Kylian Mbappe managed a brace, while Bradley Barcola and Ousmane Dembele found the scoresheet for France, although their strikes counted for naught in the grand scheme of things.

Sports.title: Pedro Porro's private life and allegation of cheating with ex-Chelsea star's girlfriend
Sports.content:
Pedro Porro's private life and allegation of cheating with ex-Chelsea star's girlfriend

Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has been one of Spain's standout performers at the World Cup, but his life off the field has also made headlines

View 7 Images Tottenham defender Pedro Porro was once forced to deny having an affair with Joao Felix's girlfriend Magui Corceiro

Tottenham Hotspur's Pedro Porro is one of the standout defenders at the World Cup this summer. The 26-year-old has arguably been the best right-back at the tournament since replacing Marcos Llorente after Spain's dismal 0-0 opening game draw with Cape Verde.

‌



Porro has stepped up and contributed by playing the entirety of five out of the six matches, during which he has scored two goals. One of those came in the semi-final victory over France, where he earned a man of the match award for his heroics.

‌



Whatever the result in the final against Argentina, this will undoubtedly go down as his breakout tournament, with Spurs likely receiving considerable interest in their full-back once it concludes.

‌



Now, Mirror Football takes a look at Porro's equally fascinating life beyond the pitch, specifically his current girlfriend and allegations of an affair involving another famous footballer's partner, which he was forced to deny.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Spain star's brutal comment about Michael Olise in dressing room after World Cup victory READ MORE :

Sensational Spain dominate France to reach World Cup final and set up possible England rematch READ MORE :

Affair rumours

In 2022, Porro denied reports that he was romantically involved with Joao Felix's then-partner, Margarida (Magui) Corceiro. At the time, Porro was playing football for Sporting Lisbon, where actress Corceiro and then-Atletico Madrid star Felix were from.

‌



The stunning model, who would later go on to start a relationship with future F1 world champion Lando Norris in 2023, fuelled speculation that she had been unfaithful to Felix with Porro after allegedly being spotted kissing the full-back in the VIP section of a Lisbon nightclub — while still in a three-year relationship with the Portugal striker.

The previous day, Porro had already set tongues wagging by ignoring several young Sporting supporters at the end of the final fixture of the season to hand his match-worn shirt directly to Corceiro, before pulling her in for a hug.

7 View 7 Images Magui Corceiro was in a relationship with Joao Felix (Image: AFP via Getty Images) 7 View 7 Images Corceiro is a fan of Sporting Lisbon in Portugal (Image: magui_corceiro / Instagram)

‌



Porro, who was single at the time, shot down claims that Sporting fan Corceiro had been unfaithful, yet oddly admitted that he shared a "special relationship" with the stunning blonde. He said: "The situation that is happening yesterday and today is very uncomfortable... I have a special relationship with her, no one is being unfaithful to anyone.

"My image is not going to be stained by anything and less by things like these. I can do whatever I want. Stop staining the image of the three of us because it is not like that."

Corceiro herself insisted the two were nothing more than close friends, having first crossed paths several months earlier at a group dinner. She was adamant that, had she wished to be unfaithful, she would not have done so in full view of an entire nightclub.

‌



"If I wanted to be kissing someone, in an intimate moment, it would not be in Lust In Rio, much less in the VIP area with that little balcony and in view of the entire nightclub," she said when asked about the allegations. "I also don't understand why those gentlemen who took the initiative to record that video and report it in such a nice way didn't remember to record me talking and hugging the other people who were there, the other guys, the players.

7 View 7 Images Margarida is an actress and model (Image: magui_corceiro/Instagram) 7 View 7 Images Corceiro denied the rumours (Image: magui_corceiro/Instagram)

‌



"Because if we want to talk about Magui Corceiro always with the players, and that this is a scene, there was a lot of material." Corceiro then followed up on her furious response with a very blunt and categorical statement of: "There were no kisses, there was nothing."

She continued: "I have just begun to understand the proportions that this is taking. It's getting out of control, and it's leaving me in a very boring position, and Joao too. On the one hand, I feel ridiculous for giving justifications to people who don't know me at all, but you guys are not understanding what's going on.

"This is being surreal, the messages that they are sending, they are sending death threats... people are crazy. I met Porro a few months ago unexpectedly at a group dinner and since then we have had a great time, we are very good friends, I love him, he is incredible and the people who know him know him very well."

‌



Felix and Corceiro officially announced their breakup in June 2023, with the forward having moved to Chelsea that January. Following an unsuccessful loan spell at AC Milan, Felix joined Saudi club Al-Nassr in 2025.

Girlfriend's World Cup support

7 View 7 Images Maria Hurtado is the mother of Porro's child (Image: mhurtado5/Instagram) 7 View 7 Images Hurtado has attended all of Porro's matches for Spain at the World Cup (Image: mhurtado5/Instagram)

‌



Porro drew a line under the entire episode after completing his move to Spurs in January 2023. Since late 2023, he has been in a relationship with Maria Hurtado.

In September 2025, the pair welcomed their first child together, a baby boy. Porro reportedly also helps raise Hurtado's daughter from a previous relationship. The brunette beauty lives with the Spurs star in north London, where she regularly shares fashion and lifestyle snaps on Instagram.

She has amassed 22,500 followers on the platform and has shared numerous pictures of herself cheering on Porro at his World Cup games this summer alongside her children. Porro appeared to dedicate his goal against France to her with a love heart-shaped hand gesture.

Article continues below

Hurtado shared a photo of the celebration, together with pictures of the couple sharing a kiss after the final whistle, with the caption: "We are so proud of you. One more step and no matter what, you've already made history," along with a love heart.

Sports.title: Argentina players refuse to give Falklands banner back after England World Cup controversy
Sports.content:
Argentina players refuse to give Falklands banner back after England World Cup controversy

Argentina players have refused to return the controversial Falkland Islands banner to the fan who smuggled it into the World Cup semi-final against England

View 2 Images Argentina players celebrated with the banner following the win over England. (Image: MB Media, Getty Images)

The Argentine fan who created the controversial Falkland Islands banner is reported to have had a request denied to have it returned to him. England lost 2-1 to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final in Atlanta on Wednesday night, missing out on the opportunity to face Spain in Sunday’s final at MetLife Stadium.

‌



There was controversy after the game in Georgia after some members of the Argentina squad unfurled a banner which read: “Las Malvinas son Argentinas,” which translates to "The Falklands are Argentine" in English.

‌



Argentina refer to the Falklands as Mavinas, and the unfurling of the banner has led to plenty of backlash across the football and political world.

‌



The banner has been deemed to be offensive by many, with 255 British soldiers losing their lives during the Falklands War in 1982. The UK Government released a statement in response to the scenes, declaring: "The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are."

BBC's Joe Hart in bizarre video before World Cup final with pundit DRENCHED in monsoon weather READ MORE :

Spain star calls out Donald Trump and confirms if he'll shake his hand at World Cup final READ MORE :

The banner's creator, identified only as Santiago to protect his identity, has revealed how he managed to deliver the banner to the Argentina players inside the Atlanta stadium.

Santiago claims he created the banner using a hotel bedsheet and paint bought from a nearby shop before stuffing it down his trousers to smuggle it inside the ground.

‌



"When I saw [Gonzalo] Montiel, I threw it to him and he caught it. He passed it to [Giovani] Lo Celso, who was the first to hold it up,” Santiago told Perfil, via the Buenos Aires Times.

He continued: "When I saw Lo Celso open it up and his teammates holding it on the pitch, I felt a joy I can't put into words – how could a piece of bedsheet mean so much to every Argentine.”

"It was crazy. I never imagined that flag would go around the world because of a silly idea we had in a hotel room," Santiago added.

‌



View 2 Images Argentina players unfurled the banner after beating England in the World Cup semi-final (Image: Getty )

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Santiago is said to have subsequently submitted a request to Claudio Tapia, president of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), seeking the return of the banner.

‌



Yet Santiago was reportedly told that "the boys don't want to give it back."

FIFA moved to address the backlash surrounding the banner by announcing an investigation will take place.

"As is standard procedure, FIFA's independent Disciplinary Committee is currently assessing the match reports and considering the relevant circumstances before deciding on potential further steps," FIFA's statement read.

‌



Despite this, the White House has insisted the Argentine players were exercising a First Amendment right to freedom of expression when they made their Falklands protest.

Argentina are set to face Spain in the World Cup final in New Jersey on Sunday evening, with both sides remaining undefeated throughout all seven of their matches in the competition, including the group stages.

Sports.title: Heartbreaking reason Spain star Lamine Yamal's dad won't attend World Cup final
Sports.content:
Heartbreaking reason Spain star Lamine Yamal's dad won't attend World Cup final

Lamine Yamal is looking to outgun Lionel Messi in the World Cup final as Spain collide with Argentina for the biggest prize in football

View 2 Images Lamine Yamal with his dad Mounir Nasraoui after winning Euro 2024 with Spain

Lamine Yamal's father will not attend the World Cup final in person - as he hasn't been able to end any match all tournament.

‌



Mounir Nasraoui has revealed he did not feel fit to travel this summer due to his health. It means Nasraoui is set to cheer on the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar from home.

‌



He explained: "I'm an epileptic. I have to take a lot of medication every day, and I can have an epilepsy seizure.

‌



"I could be here, right now, under the effects of stress or emotion, and have a seizure without realising it. So you always have to think things through carefully.

"Before traveling, you have to think about me, about him, and about all the people around us, you know? I might end up causing problems. So it's better to stay home and watch all this from here."

Spain and Argentina World Cup final training plans rocked by electrical thunderstorms READ MORE :

Spain star Aymeric Laporte calls out Argentina over England World Cup antics READ MORE :

Around a month after Yamal's last major tournament, Euro 2024 - which he won, dad Mounir was stabbed in a parking lot. The authorities arrested four people in connection with the incident.

‌



He remains very close to his family despite his superstardom. His brother Keyne, who is three years old, has been one of the heroes of this World Cup due to his celebrations in the stands.

"I come from an apartment where the kitchen and the bedroom were the same space," Yamal recently stated, citing his humble beginnings.

"I see my mother happy, I see that my brother can have the childhood I would have liked to have, and that's what makes me happiest."

‌



View 2 Images Mounir Nasraoui, the father of Lamine Yamal, suffers with epilepsy

Fatima, Yamal's paternal grandmother, left Morocco on a bus that she wasn't legally allowed to board. She would work shifts just so her son could join before he ended up having Yamal as a teenager.

Now that 19-year-old is about to walk out on the biggest stage of all. While Yamal's parents split when he was three, his football career took off soon after.

‌



He joined Barcelona's youth ranks at seven, though he was actually scouted at the age of seven and at the age of 15, he made his big breakthrough into the first-team.

In doing so, he became the youngest player to make their debut for the Catalan giants since way back in 1922.

Yamal has scored just one goal at this World Cup but after shaking off a thigh issue, he is expected to start against Argentina as he looks to add a second international trophy to his cabinet.

Sports.title: Antonelli takes big Belgian GP win as Russell's woes deepen after Hamilton clash
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli overcame an unfortunately timed Virtual Safety Car to overtake Charles Leclerc and win the Belgian Grand Prix on a day team-mate George Russell's title hopes suffered a major fresh blow.

Antonelli doubled his in-house advantage over Russell to 50 points after the Briton was spun out into the gravel at the fifth corner of the first lap in a collision that stewards judged Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton had been at fault for.

Hamilton was given a five-second penalty, which he served at his sole pit stop, and eventually finished fourth after overtaking McLaren's Oscar Piastri late on.

But Hamilton is under a post-race investigation for an alleged unsafe Ferrari release at the same pit stop after he was given the signal to leave the box and knocked over a mechanic who was still trying to work on his car's front wing.

The mechanic was struck by the Ferrari's front-right tyre and was briefly knocked to his knees before being helped back up to his feet before Hamilton fully exited the pit box.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ferrari pit crew were unable to attach Lewis Hamilton's front wing as the British driver also knocked over a mechanic after being given the green light

Hamilton moves back ahead of Russell in second to Antonelli in the standings - 45 points behind the Italian, with one race to go in Hungary this coming week before F1's summer break.

Max Verstappen, who briefly took the lead from Antonelli on the first lap out of Eau Rouge before the Mercedes almost immediately blasted back past, took third after he was also jumped by Leclerc during the VSC.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow

Isack Hadjar took sixth in the second Red Bull, just holding off Lando Norris on fresher tyres after the McLaren had run all the way to lap 30 on hard tyres having started a penalised 13th on the grid.

Gabriel Bortoleto was eighth for Audi ahead of Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Franco Colapinto.

Sports.title: Russell blames Mercedes power issue for collision with Hamilton
Sports.content:
George Russell says a power issue with his Mercedes was to blame for leaving him vulnerable to a first-lap collision with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton that took him out of the Belgian Grand Prix.

Russell started third on the grid and retained his position through the first corner but was then passed by Hamilton and left side-by-side with McLaren's Oscar Piastri as they came to the end of the lengthy Kemmel Straight.

Russell broke late and attempted to reclaim third back around the outside of Hamilton, but the pair made contact which spun the Mercedes into the gravel and out of the race.

Despite Hamilton being given a five-second penalty by the stewards for causing the collision, Russell told Sky Sports F1 he was more frustrated with his car than his former team-mate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell pointed to an issue with the car as a reason for his collision with Lewis Hamilton during the Belgian GP

"I just got totally swallowed up down the straight," said Russell, who dropped 50 points behind his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli after the championship leader won the race.

"I lost three positions down the straight down into Turn Five and then the incident was a racing incident.

"Maybe I could have gone a bit wider, maybe he (Hamilton) could have braked a bit more. The incident shouldn't have happened if I had the speed down the straight.

"Very, very disappointed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix

The incident came after Russell had bemoaned a lack of power costing him in qualifying on Saturday, when he was more than half a second off pole-sitter Antonelli in fourth.

Russell has appeared confused in recent weeks as to what is causing him to generally be unable to match Antonelli's pace.

He said on Thursday's media day at Spa that he was working on changing his driving style as he believes that was costing him time in 2026's new generation of cars, but on Saturday revealed that he had changed his mind and no longer thought his driving style was the issue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell discusses his recent struggles with the Mercedes car and the gap between himself and teammate Kimi Antonelli

Asked how Mercedes can get to the bottom of the issue, Russell added: "I appreciate everyone is working hard to solve the problem, but I'm stood here [in the TV interview pen] on lap five of the race.

"It felt like I was in a good position to fight for the lead up to Turn One and then, suddenly, no power and it's all gone."

Sports.title: Tokaido takes on two in the Prix Robert Papin
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Sunday with action from Newton Abbot and Chantilly, live on Sky Sports Racing...

12.58 Chantilly - Tokaido faces King Of Cloughan and Beibhinn

A classy field of three head to post for this Group Two Prix Robert Papin at Chantilly.

Amy Murphy saddles Tokaido who recorded a third success on his fourth outing when comfortably claiming the Group Three Prix du Bois under Tony Piccone. That was his first try at six-furlongs and his connections are expecting him to handle this step up in class.

Joseph O'Brien is double handed with King Of Cloughan the pick. A son of St Mark's Basilica, he built on his first couple of starts to take the Windsor Castle Stakes at the Royal meeting. Only on top late on, he will appreciate a decent pace here under new rider Pierre-Charles Boudot.

Beibhinn landed a Listowel maiden on her second start before an excellent third in this grade at the Curragh so cannot be discounted.

4.35 Chantily - Exciting Erdenali bids to remain unbeaten

Erdenali looks to extend his winning run in an excellent Group Three Prix Messidor at 4.35pm.

Francis-Henri Graffard's gelding is unbeaten in all three starts having burst onto the scene at Saint-Cloud back in March. He takes another step up the ladder here but could prove equal to the test and remains a highly promising prospect.
