Sports.title: Lionel Messi faces heir apparent Lamine Yamal in the World Cup final: The father-son symbolism could not be stronger as Argentina star comes up against a generation of players who idolised him, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
How much is David Beckham set to pocket from his World Cup brand deals? Take on our quiz in our newsletter HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Les Miserables is playing at Radio City Music Hall this week. There are rumours Thomas Tuchel and his tactics board are set for a special guest appearance. Ariana Grande is at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn. Jon Bon Jovi is at Madison Square Garden, Noah Kahan's at Citi Field in Queens.

At Carnegie Hall on W57th Street, there will be a recital by the Washington International Rachmaninoff Music Competition Winners. At the Broadway Theatre, there is a musical production of The Great Gatsby. The New York Yankees are hosting the LA Dodgers. Death of a Salesman is playing at the Winter Garden Theater on Broadway.

But the main event of the weekend is taking place on the other side of the Hudson River. The World Cup final, the 104th and last match of a protracted, mammoth tournament that has stretched across three huge countries, will take place in the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday afternoon.

If it were on Broadway, they'd call it All His Sons. Because this might be a tie between Argentina and Spain but it is also a meeting between Lionel Messi, the greatest football player the world has ever seen, and a generation of Spain players who grew up revering him, a generation of players who have been inspired by him.

In a way, we are all Messi's sons, those of us who love football, even those of us who are 20 years older than him. For two decades and more, he has made us feel lucky that we live in the era in which he has played and that we have been enchanted by the magic he has worked.

Messi is 39 years old and this will be the last World Cup game of his incredible career. So there will be poignancy attached to the final, too, because no one wants to see him go, no one wants to lose his artistry and his genius.

Lionel Messi cradles five-month old Lamine Yamal in 2007. On Sunday they will be on opposite sides in the World Cup final

Messi pictured with Dani Olmo, who will also be hoping to topple Argentina with Spain

Even amid the bleak disappointment of England's defeat to Argentina in Wednesday's semi-final in Atlanta, it was possible to acknowledge that Messi's run and right-foot cross to set up the winning goal for Lautaro Martinez was a verse of poetry.

The final will come to be seen as his crowning moment if Argentina become the first team since Brazil in 1958 and 1962 to win back-to-back World Cups. Many in his home country consider him the equal to Diego Maradona but if Messi wins a second World Cup, it will elevate him to a different level.

But whether Argentina win or lose, it will be a final heavy with the symbolism of the passage of time. Messi's reign is almost over and the man many have anointed his heir, Lamine Yamal, will be playing on the opposite side.

Messi is more than twice Yamal's age and it will be the first time they have met on the pitch. At the final whistle, it will be Donald Trump and his stooge, Gianni Infantino, who present the World Cup trophy but it will be Messi who passes the torch.

Between Messi and Yamal, the father-son symbolism could hardly be stronger. It is captured most obviously in a picture taken of the two of them in 2007 when Messi was a shy, callow, 20-year-old who was just breaking into the Barcelona first team and Yamal was still a babe in arms.

Several other members of this Spain squad - including Dani Olmo, Gavi and Joan Garcia - also had their pictures taken with Messi as children before they would go on to become senior Barcelona players.

The photoshoot with Yamal took place in the away dressing room at Barcelona's Camp Nou stadium after Yamal's parents, Morocco-born Mounir Nasraoui and Sheila Ebana from Equatorial Guinea, entered a raffle run by Catalan newspaper Sport where the winners would have photos taken of their baby with a Barcelona player.

Yamal's family were among the winners and they were paired with Messi. In the shoot, Messi was pictured bathing the five-month-old Yamal and then holding him, wrapped in a towel. Now that baby boy is a young man who turned 19 last week and has been spoken about widely as the successor to Messi.

The comparisons are irresistible, partly because of the picture, partly because Yamal has followed the same route as Messi, coming up through the club's La Masia academy and announcing his prodigious talent early. So far, Yamal is ahead of the curve Messi's career travelled.

Spain midfielder Gavi, 21, with Messi before he went on to play for Barcelona

Spain goalkeeper Joan Garcia, who moved from Espanyol to Barca, pictured with Messi

By his 19th birthday Messi had scored 11 first team goals and won La Liga and the Champions League. At the same stage, Yamal has already scored 56 goals, won the European Championships with Spain in 2024, won La Liga three times and the Copa del Rey once. He is setting a fearsome pace.

Is he set to become Messi's successor as the best player on the planet? Well, Kylian Mbappe might have something to say about that. In fact, there has been talk of the torch being passed before, when Mbappe inspired France to their World Cup final victory in Russia in 2018 and, again, when he scored a hat-trick in the 2022 World Cup final before a penalty shoot-out defeat to Messi and Argentina.

Mbappe had also looked like the best player in this tournament – and is tied with Messi in the race for the Golden Boot on eight goals – until France were so rudely defenestrated by Spain in their semi-final in Dallas on Tuesday.

But Mbappe has never quite been able to establish himself as the undisputed new king. His club career has been bedevilled by political wrangling and he is still to win the Champions League.

That is something also missing from the CV of Harry Kane, who had such a stellar season with Bayern Munich that he had a claim to be the world's best. Six goals in this tournament, going into last night's third place play-off with France, has not harmed his cause.

But Yamal is a prodigy. He made his debut for Barcelona when he was 15, the youngest player ever to wear the shirt for the first team, and he can do things on the ball that take the breath away. Sometimes, he looks a couple of levels above anyone else on the pitch, which is Messi's habitual state of grace.

Yamal tore a hamstring during a Barcelona game against Celta Vigo at the end of April and has not yet been at his scintillating best in this tournament. But he looked closer to that level in the victory over France, a victory so comprehensive that Spain are clear favourites to win the final.

The match will pit the reigning European champions against the reigning South American champions, it will pit Messi against Yamal and it will pit Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni against the man he regards as a mentor, Spain coach Luis de la Fuente. Both coaches, by the way, graduated from age group teams within the national set-up, a route England chose to ignore when they appointed Tuchel.

Spain have a very different identity to most of the sides Argentina have faced so far in this tournament. Time and again, Argentina have recovered from adversity but if they go behind against Spain, Spain will not lose their nerve as Tuchel and England did in Atlanta on Wednesday night.

Spain are a possession-based team. They have the best defence in the tournament and in Rodri, who has been playing with the same authority he had before he tore his anterior cruciate ligament playing for Manchester City in September 2024, they have the best defensive midfielder in the tournament.

Their performance against France, dominant, patient, relentless, penetrating, was a template of how they perform at their best. They keep the ball and when they lose it, they fight aggressively to retrieve it fast. They have averaged 63.7 per cent possession in their seven matches so far.

Their movement is dynamic and intricate. England showed in spells that Argentina are vulnerable in defence, particularly down the flanks and Spain have the talent to exploit that. Tuchel said it was not in England's DNA to retain possession. Whether that is true or not, Spain are the best in the world at it.

Yamal will be hoping to deny Messi a second consecutive World Cup triumph in New Jersey

They will also be up against the most cussed side in the world. If England are masters at finding ways to lose the biggest matches, Argentina have proved in this tournament that that thrive when the odds are stacked against them. Time and again – against Cape Verde, against Egypt, against Switzerland and against England – they have found a way to win when the match seemed to be swinging away from them.

They can be a dogged, spiteful, unpleasant force, typified by Enzo Fernandez, who often plays with the malevolent energy of a reconstructed thug. They give no quarter. And they are utterly dedicated to the idea of providing Messi with the vehicle to take him to a second World Cup triumph.

'For the Malvinas, for Diego and for Leo's last one,' the blue and white hordes chant at Argentina's games. Only 90 minutes of Messi's World Cup career remain. Only 90 minutes until he claims a second World Cup trophy or retires from the international game with one. Only 90 minutes until he passes the torch and one, from all his sons, reaches out to take it.

Sports.title: 'Numb' George Russell's Formula One world championship dream plunges into jeopardy as Kimi Antonelli seizes on team-mate's opening lap crash with Lewis Hamilton to take commanding lead after Belgian Grand Prix win
Sports.content:
'Numb' George Russell's Formula One world championship dream plunges into jeopardy as Kimi Antonelli seizes on team-mate's opening lap crash with Lewis Hamilton to take commanding lead after Belgian Grand Prix win

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

George Russell claimed he is 'numb to disappointment' but his pained face told a different story after his first lap collision with Lewis Hamilton ended his participation in the Belgian Grand Prix.

Poor George is growing accustomed to summoning words to describe slings and Silver Arrows of outrageous fortune he cannot fully comprehend.

His world championship dream is in jeopardy and questions fill his bamboozled mind. He cannot find answers for all that is assailing him. Why is he not as fast as Kimi Antonelli, the race winner and championship leader, in the same Mercedes machinery?

Why is he suffering dramatic losses of pace in a straight line? Why are all the expectations he embraced as the pre-season championship favourite eluding him week after week?

The story of his cameo at Spa nailed those doubts further into his psyche. Starting third he was cleanly away – 'a great first corner', as he noted wryly – before he was practically reduced to running on the spot along the Kemmel Straight.

He slipped back to sixth, as if stuck in treacle, as he entered Les Combes, the right-left combination. He was fractionally ahead of Hamilton's Ferrari at this stage, but they were overlapping.

George Russell crashed out of the Belgian Grand Prix after colliding with Lewis Hamilton

Russell was sent into the gravel after being clipped by the Ferrari in the opening lap in Spa

Sunday's result serves as a major blow to Russell's championship hopes

His rear-right entangled itself with Hamilton's front-left. Russell spun around into the gravel, where he was beached. He held his gloved palms open in an expression of agony in the cockpit. He climbed out unhurt physically, though seriously wounded again between the ears.

Hamilton was handed a harsh five-second penalty for his part in the clumsy footwork, but went on to finish fourth. That meant that the seven-time world champion leapfrogged Russell as Antonelli's closest challenger, 45 points back. Russell is 50 from the top. It was the third time in 10 races that he had failed to finish.

'For whatever reason the battery decided not to recharge at Turn One,' explained a nonplussed Russell.

'I exited the first corner 35 per cent down. Because of that, and it didn't charge, I had a boost problem. The turbo didn't sort itself out, so no power, and I got to the top of Eau Rouge with zero per cent battery and quite frankly it was dangerous.

'I got swamped by three cars and I shouldn't have been in that position in the first place. It is why I am most angry. The incident with Lewis was a racing incident.

'He was more to blame than I was. But he didn't do anything reckless or on purpose.

'I had been ready to fight the two guys ahead of me up to Turn Five.

'It was a different problem from yesterday… but it is something every day now.

'I am numb to disappointment. When it happens so often you just get used to it.'

It has been a story of setback after setback for Russell this season. His reverses are compounded by Antonelli, just 19, growing in confidence every race, and he has hardly lacked for it since he registered his first win in China, the second staging post of the 22-race season.

Russell's specific complaint here centred on why he is suddenly losing power when Antonelli is not. Indeed, when the rest of the field are not, certainly not so dramatically as he is.

Mercedes have no ready answers. Will they find solutions ahead of Budapest coming next weekend?

While Russell was in the paddock, Antonelli was in clear command on the track. His only concern came when a Virtual Safety Car, brought about by debris, permitted the Ferraris a cheap stop. Charles Leclerc lucked into the lead at this point.

But the Italian made the decisive pass on the Kemmel Straight with 10 laps remaining, and that was victory No 6 of 2025 secured. Leclerc took second place, ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

Hamilton's day was eventful. Having survived his skirmish with Russell unscathed, he and Leclerc went wheel-to-wheel soon afterwards. They nearly touched but did not quite. Leclerc was feisty, as he also showed in a brush with McLaren's Oscar Piastri in which he (Leclerc) was fortunate to escape without censure when they touched.

Hamilton pitted with Leclerc and served his penalty there and then. That done, he was given the green light to go. The mechanic holding the gun on the front-left tyre was still in his path, for some reason.

His right knee was caught by the accelerating Ferrari. He will have a purple bruise to sport but was otherwise unharmed.

Hamilton, who asked after his man's welfare, was due to face the stewards afterwards on the charge of unsafe release (verdict pending).

Piastri came home fifth, a place ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar and two in front of defending world champion Lando Norris, the old pal who maiden title success Russell is trying to emulate. If only he could get a break.

Sports.title: England stars are home: Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions land in Birmingham after seven-week World Cup journey ended with best result since 1966 after Argentina heartbreak
Sports.content:
England stars are home: Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions land in Birmingham after seven-week World Cup journey ended with best result since 1966 after Argentina heartbreak

How much is David Beckham set to pocket from his World Cup brand deals? Take on our quiz in our newsletter HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England arrived back home from the World Cup on Sunday afternoon, after they finished their seven-week journey on a high in Miami.

The Three Lions fell short of winning football's ultimate prize for the first time since 1966 after losing their semi-final 2-1 to Argentina on Wednesday, but restored pride with a thrilling 6-4 win over France in the bronze final.

Their victory in the Sunshine State meant they secured their best World Cup performance since their triumph 60 years ago.

The manner of Wedesday's defeat, in which the Three Lions crumbled after taking the lead through Anthony Gordon, has led to increased scrutiny on manager Thomas Tuchel, who was hired to navigate the team through high-pressure matches after Gareth Southgate fell short during his tenure.

Tuchel said the widespread criticism aimed in his direction after the Argentina result felt as though England had been eliminated during the group stage.

Tuchel said: ‘The press conference yesterday [before the France win] felt as if we went out in group stage without a win, to be very honest.

‘Twenty-four hours later we had our biggest success in 60 years. I think the low and the drama about what happened against Argentina was too low, but that's part of it.

'The best thing you can do is react on the pitch and get the next win, everything else is just talking. Talking doesn't get you points. Talking doesn't get you wins. So you have to endure it. You have to hold it and be strong and keep believing. I’m glad that we showed that reaction. It’s very impressive.’

Tuchel does not believe he has lost the faith of England’s supporters either, as he added: ‘I don't think that I lost the trust. Whatever happened in the final 30 minutes against Argentina, why it happened, whatever happened in the last 10 minutes, we were close, but it's my job to take decisions. My decisions, my interventions, my substitutions, the change of structure.

England are home after touching down in Birmingham following their World Cup journey

The Three Lions failed to win the World Cup after a seven-week adventure in the United States

The stars were whisked away from Birmingham Airport after landing on Sunday afternoon

'It did not have the effect that I wanted, so I have to live with this. It’s very painful for me because I did it in good faith. I did it with a clear plan and a clear idea behind it. It didn't work out so I take the blame and the responsibility.

‘But I strongly believe that we built more in this World Cup than we can lose in these 30 minutes, and me personally for a decision that turns out not to be effective. The pain will stay with me. The scar will stay with me and with the players and no one else.

'In the end, we need to win the trust on a daily basis in international football. In seven, eight weeks we're back together, it's Nations League. We need to win the trust and build the trust. It's never a given, so this is normal in a high-level sport that you have to prove yourself, you have to prove a point every single time that you compete.’

England spent the bulk of their World Cup journey stationed in Kansas City, and played matches in Dallas, Boston, New York, Atlanta, Mexico City and Miami.

Sports.title: NYC flooding horror brings travel chaos just as 80,000 set out for World Cup Final at MetLife Stadium
Sports.content:
How much is David Beckham set to pocket from his World Cup brand deals? Take on our quiz in our newsletter HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

New York has been hit by heavy floods ahead of the World Cup final, leaving hundreds of fans at risk of missing the showdown, as the United States battles the conditions for one final time this tournament.

Spain and Argentina will face off in the final of the competition this evening, with the game to be held at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, roughly five miles from New York City.

Much of the focus at the tournament has been on the weather, with France and England both seeing games delayed due to nature - be it extreme heat or lightning warnings.

And, for one final time, doubt has been cast over the kick-off time of the final this evening, which is set for 3pm ET (8pm BST).

The streets of New York were flooded on the eve of the tournament's finale, with heavy rain causing mayhem. Cars were submerged and pedestrians were seen walking through chest-high water.

Between two and four inches of rain are said to have fallen, with a tornado warning also issued.

New York City has been hit by severe floods just hours before the World Cup final

A motorist said they waited up to 20 minutes for flood water near MetLife Stadium in New Jersey to recede before driving through

A flood watch covering eastern Bergen County, where MetLife is located, northeastern New Jersey and New York City remained in effect until 2am Sunday.

Although the heaviest rain had moved south and east by late Saturday afternoon, the National Weather Service warned that further storms could produce rainfall rates of one to two inches per hour.

The final showstopper between Spain and Argentina will be able to go ahead unaffected - but many fans may miss out.

While the worst of the horrific weather had passed by Sunday morning, leaving blue skies in its wake, the torrential conditions of the previous day left mayhem in its wake.

The dangerous conditions caused further turmoil at the region’s three major airports wreaking havoc for the thousands descending on New York and New Jersey where 80,000 fans are expected to fill MetLife Stadium for Sunday's final.

Hundreds of flights into the New York area from across the United States were rocked by delays, or worse, cancellations as the downpours compounded travel problems.

The Federal Aviation Administration ordered multiple ground stops at LaGuardia, JFK and Newark, until at least 5pm ET on Saturday due to the thunderstorms.

Meanwhile, the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway was flooded, leaving drivers stranded on the washed-out roadway. Many sought safety on the roofs or bonnets of their vehicles as the water in some areas rose as high as car windows.

Former England goalkeeper and BBC pundit showed off the conditions on social media

An FDNY fire truck was captured wading through the flooding - the water almost reaching its windscreen - to rescue the drivers. Firefighters assisted New Yorkers slowly inch their way along a ledge to dry land.

At around 10am ET, the queues to enter MetLife Stadium had already begun snaking through the parking lot with hundreds of media members, security staff and volunteers already making their way into the ground five hours before kickoff.

There had been calls to move the World Cup final and, while conditions are starting to improve, severe thunderstorm warnings remain for parts of New Jersey.

New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani posted on social media: 'Don't risk your safety in these dangerous conditions. – Exercise caution while traveling.

'Take public transit whenever possible. Never walk, bike, or drive through floodwaters. No destination is worth risking your safety.'

It is understood, however, that there are hopes there will be no delay to tonight's proceedings.

The downpours presented a lone benefit with the deluge of rain expected to help clear Canadian wildfire smoke from the air.

An air-quality health advisory remained in effect across New York City until midnight Saturday after fine-particle pollution pushed the Air Quality Index above 100.

Meteorologists interviewed by the Associated Press said the storms should improve air quality from unhealthy to moderate before kickoff.

Colas interminables para acceder al MetLife Stadium a más de cinco horas para el comienzo del partido.



De momento solo prensa, seguridad y voluntarios pueden entrar al recinto.



🇪🇸🇦🇷El España-Argentina se juega a las 21:00h, pero se vive desde las 18:00h en @la1_tve y… pic.twitter.com/BQEBKdz1TY — Teledeporte (@teledeporte) July 19, 2026

The final will be held at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, roughly five miles from New York

Hundreds of Argentina descended on Times Square once the torrential rain had cleared

On Saturday, New York residents received an alert from the National Weather Service, branding conditions 'a life threatening situation'.

It read: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3.30pm EDT,' it read.

'This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.'

The New York Yankees' baseball game against the Dodgers at Yankee Stadium was cancelled on Saturday due to the weather, but it is set to be rescheduled for this afternoon.

Former England goalkeeper Joe Hart, who has been working as a pundit for BBC throughout the tournament, has been in New York and highlighted the struggles prior to kick-off.

Hart and the likes of Wayne Rooney had been based in Salford until the BBC opted to end their work from home World Cup ahead of England's semi-final defeat by Argentina.

'Weather's absolutely banging here. Shoes are off, trainers are ruined', Hart said in a video he shared to Instagram. He could be seen walking in heavy rain, drenched.

Argentina's training session was delayed by 45 minutes on Saturday, while Spain's flight from Kansas to New York was also delayed.

Sports.title: England and France players involved in prayer huddle just moments after their epic World Cup third-place play-off in Miami
Sports.content:
England and France's footballers put rivalry aside after their 10-goal thriller in Miami on Saturday night to share a poignant moment of unity on the pitch.

Seven players from both national sides stood together shoulder to shoulder to form a ring and bow their heads in collective prayer just moments after their World Cup epic.

The players involved in the centre circle gathering were England's hat-trick hero Bukayo Saka, Arsenal's Eberechi Eze, Trevoh Chalobah of Chelsea, Marc Guehi of Manchester City, Jean-Philippe Mateta and Maxence Lacroix of Crystal Palace and Bayern Munich's Dayot Upamecano.

The moving scene was shared widely across social media, drawing plaudits from supporters of both teams and beyond.

Though this show of faith is not common among opposing teams on the pitch, it plays an important part in football.

Last year Arsenal and England star Noni Madueke revealed how he and nine of his team-mates pray together and go through bible scripture before matches.

Bukayo Saka, Eberechi Eze, Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Guehi, Jean-Philippe Mateta, Maxence Lacroix and Dayot Upamecano share a prayer on the pitch in Miami on Saturday night

Bukayo Saka (centre) netted a hat-trick to help England secure their best World Cup finish since 1966

After defeat by Argentina on Wednesday, England competed with 'broken hearts' to claim third place in Miami

Daily Mail Sport reported how the Premier League's 'Bible Boys' - the term used by fans on social media to describe the Arsenal squad - were openly voicing their faith as they rode divine inspiration to the title.

That includes a group of their Christian players meeting to pray either in an onsite dedicated prayer room - opened by former Gunners midfielder Mohamed Elneny, a devout Muslim - or in a quiet room near the changing room.

Full back Jurrien Timber is among the most open about his faith, regularly posting Bible verses on X on the morning of the north London club's matches.

And Madueke is just as passionate.

He said: 'It's fantastic that we have a squad that is not ashamed of that (practising religion). We believe it gives us such a massive boost when we go on to the pitch, that we're not alone.

'On the pitch we have got each other but we believe we have God fighting for us as well, so I feel like it's fantastic. It just brings us closer together.

England star Noni Madueke (left) has spoken of the importance of faith in Arsenal's success

At Arsenal, religion isn’t hidden away - with players like Eze free to practise their faith with their team-mates

'Before every game we pray together for a few minutes and then also at the hotel, for a few minutes, studying the bible and just praying.

'Not even just always praying, just seeing if we're all good, checking on each other, stuff like that. It's top.'

In Miami on Saturday night it was England who prevailed in the third-place play-off to earn their bronze medals after a bewildering 90 minutes of action ended in a barely-believable 6-4 final scoreline.

Reeling from their agonising semi-final defeat by Argentina just three days earlier, a much-changed England side raced into a four-goal lead by half-time after goals from Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and two from Saka.

Saka completed his hat-trick from the penalty spot in the second half, but only after Les Bleus had staged an incredible comeback.

Kylian Mbappe was unable to help France finish on a high in an eye-popping end to both nations' World Cup journey

Kylian Mbappe - who moved two ahead of Lionel Messi in the race for the Golden Boot - nabbed a brace as Bradley Barcola also scored to give Thomas Tuchel's side a scare.

France gave themselves renewed belief during seven frantic minutes of stoppage time as Ousmane Dembele netted to make it 5-4 to England.

But their hopes of a sensational comeback were dashed when Jude Bellingham embarked on a barnstorming solo run to slot home and secure England's best World Cup finish in 60 years.

And it meant that Didier Deschamps tasted defeat in his final game in charge of France after 14 years at the helm.

Sports.title: Hannah Rapp dead at 26: US boxer killed by car when driver passed by then REVERSED into her in Texas
Sports.content:
US boxer Hannah Rapp has died after she was hit by a car while cycling in Texas on Saturday.

The Brazos County Sheriff's Office says Rapp, 26, was cycling on a highway when she was passed by a car which suddenly came to a stop and then reversed into her.

She received treatment at the scene and was then taken to hospital where she later passed away from her injuries.

The driver, who authorities have named as 31-year-old Charles Medina, has been arrested and charged with manslaughter.

'Investigators learned that the driver of the vehicle... had passed two bicyclists traveling along FM 159. After passing the bicyclists, Mr. Medina stopped his vehicle, reversed, and struck one of the cyclists,' the Sheriff's Office statement said.

'Despite lifesaving efforts, she later passed away at the hospital. At this time, investigators believe this was an isolated incident.'

American boxer Hannah Rapp has died after being hit by a car while cycling

Tributes have poured in for Rapp, 26, after the incident in Texas on early Saturday morning

Authorities added that their investigation remains ongoing. The incident happened at around 10am local time on Saturday morning in Texas, a short distance away from her local boxing gym.

Rapp had enjoyed a burgeoning career in the ring and challenged for the WBC women's featherweight title on June 13, losing to Tiara Brown in Orlando.

Her professional record read eight wins, one draw and one loss.

Jake Paul, her promoter, tweeted: 'Gone too soon. Condolences to her entire clan. RIP warrior, Hannah Rapp.'

WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman said in a statement: 'She was an exceptional boxer, but above all, an invaluable member of our boxing family.'

Rapp's former rival Brown labelled her the 'best dance partner I have ever faced as a pro' and revealed how Rapp had asked for her autograph before their bout.

'It filled my heart because we were getting ready for war, yet she was still asking for my autograph,' said Brown. 'We fought a great fight. It was my honor to share the ring with her.'

Rapp, from Indiana, turned professional in 2024 and had competed in athletics before turning her attention to the sweet science.

Rapp received treatment at the scene before she later passed away in hospital in Texas

During training, she maintained a full-time job as a fire and life safety inspector.

A GoFundMe has also been launched to help her family cover the costs of funeral expenses.

'A beloved daughter to Angie and James, sister to Tanner and Maggie, a friend to everyone she met, and an inspiring boxing athlete,' the tribute read.

'Hannah was resilient. She was brave and insightful, always pushing others to do their best. She loved her family so incredibly much, and moving from Indiana to Texas meant distance for her friends and family.

'Hannah was an inspiration. Even on her hardest days, she continued to bring love, laughter, and light into the lives of others.'

Sports.title: Arsenal 'complete Tottenham transfer swoop' despite Morgan Rogers blow as player rejects rivals
Sports.content:
Arsenal 'complete Tottenham transfer swoop' despite Morgan Rogers blow as player rejects rivals

Arsenal are set to announce the signing of a youth defender from Tottenham after missing out on Aston Villa target Morgan Rogers to Chelsea

View 2 Images Elijah Upson will complete a move to Arsenal from Tottenham

Arsenal have reportedly completed the signing of Tottenham prospect Elijah Upson, the son of former Gunners defender Matthew, after missing out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea. The 18‑year‑old is understood to have turned down a new contract in north London despite spending most of his youth career in the Spurs academy.

‌



Chelsea, Manchester City and Everton were also interested, with European giants Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund and Bayer Leverkusen among his admirers. However, reports say Upson made his decision after visiting Arsenal's London Colney training ground and consulting with his family.

‌



Upson is now set to follow in the footsteps of his father Matthew, who made 56 appearances for Arsenal between 1997 and 2003. With the move expected to be confirmed in due course, Spurs will receive compensation from their rivals, reports Fabrizio Romano.

‌



The versatile defender will arrive at the Emirates with the ability to play centrally or at right‑back. Upson featured in six of Spurs' seven Uefa Youth League matches this season.

Declan Rice footage shows England star's true mentality right after carnage against France READ MORE :

He also started 13 of the Lilywhites' first 16 Under‑18 Premier League fixtures. Across the age groups, Upson made 34 appearances for the Under‑18s, six for the Under‑19s and two for the Under‑21s.

Upson's move comes after news broke that Chelsea had agreed to pay Aston Villa a club‑record £117million for Rogers. Arsenal had long appeared the most likely destination for the former Middlesbrough star but their pursuit stalled once Chelsea swooped in to strike a mega‑money deal with Villa.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 2 Images Morgan Rogers is set to finalise his move to Chelsea next week despite interest from Arsenal

Xabi Alonso played a key role in convincing the England international to choose Stamford Bridge over the Emirates, despite the Gunners being champions. Rogers is expected to undergo a medical in London on Monday once he returns from the World Cup.

‌



The transfer will trigger a major windfall for Rogers' former club, Middlesbrough, who inserted a 20 per cent sell‑on clause into the deal that took the attacking midfielder to Villa Park for an initial £7m with a further £8m in add‑ons, during the 2024 winter window.

Rogers started for England in their 6-4 win over France on Saturday night. The 23‑year‑old made three starts at the World Cup and scored twice, coming off the bench in four other games.

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton punished at Belgian GP after taking out George Russell in first-lap crash
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton punished at Belgian GP after taking out George Russell in first-lap crash

George Russell's Belgian Grand Prix came to an end inside the opening lap at Spa-Francorchamps after colliding with Lewis Hamilton and sliding into the gravel

View 2 Images George Russell is out of the Belgian Grand Prix (Image: Sky Sports)

Lewis Hamilton has been punished with a five-second penalty after crashing into George Russell at the Belgian Grand Prix. Russell, 28, retired inside the opening lap at Spa-Francorchamps after colliding with former teammate Hamilton, 41, before sliding straight into the gravel.

‌



The incident occurred at Les Combes, as, after Hamilton tried to overtake, his front wheel caught Russell's back wheel, causing the Mercedes driver to spin off the track.

‌



It caused Russell to retire from the race and a safety car was deployed. As well as that, the FIA launched an investigation into the crash with Hamilton later receiving a five-second penalty.

‌



Russell said: "I just got totally swallowed up down the straight. I lost three positions down the straight down into Turn Five and then the incident was a racing incident.

Belgian GP grid: F1 qualifying result as Lando Norris penalty changes starting grid READ MORE :

"Maybe I could have gone a bit wider, maybe he could have braked a bit more, the incident shouldn't have happened if I had the speed down the straight. Very, very disappointed."

Delivering his verdict on the incident, Sky Sports commentator David Croft said: "We have seen drivers get penalties in the past when they've had that little snap of oversteer and they've made contact with another car, and accidental or not, the stewards have given penalties for that in the past."

‌



Martin Brundle, the ex-F1 driver and Sky Sports pundit, added: "Let's see what they do. Lewis is obviously slightly nervous about it because he felt the need to get the justification over knowing that will be fed into the system.

View 2 Images George Russell retired from the Belgian Grand Prix after a crash with Lewis Hamilton (Image: Sky Sports)

"Whether they felt he lost control of his car, for me it was a racing incident. It will be frustrating for George, George unquestionably left more than a car's width on the inside so I don't think there's any finger pointing at George Russell in that but Lewis is saying 'I'm up in around the cars, it's first lap, I've lost downforce on my front wing because I'm tucked up underneath another car's gearbox and not a lot I can do about it.'

‌



"If the stewards determined that constitutes a loss of control of your car, Lewis will get a penalty."

Russell's retirement from the Belgian GP has put a huge dent into his world title hopes. Going into Spa, the Brit was second in the Drivers' Standings and 25 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli.

But, with Antonelli in pole position to win the Belgian GP and rivals including Lewis Hamilton behind him gaining points, Russell is expected to lose further ground in the race for the world title.

Sports.title: Man Utd star makes transfer statement and confirms he wants exit - 'I am ready'
Sports.content:
Man Utd star makes transfer statement and confirms he wants exit - 'I am ready'

Radek Vitek's future has been the subject of speculation during the summer transfer window but the goalkeeper was involved in Manchester United's first pre-season friendly against Wrexham

View 2 Images Radek Vitek has opened up on his future (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United goalkeeper Radek Vitek has confirmed that he wants to leave Old Trafford in order to play regular football. Vitek, 22, enjoyed an impressive season on loan at Bristol City in the Championship last term, sweeping their end-of-year awards.

‌



The Czech relished being a No.1 and wants to have the same role during the 2026-27 season. But with Senne Lammens having nailed down the position at United, he knows that he'll have to go elsewhere in order to be first choice.

‌



After playing the second half of the Red Devils' first pre-season friendly on Saturday, a 1-0 defeat to Wrexham in Helsinki, Vitek told reporters: "I feel great and ready to go again somewhere to be, hopefully, number one, so we will see. We will see what is going to happen.

‌



"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so. I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete."

Thomas Tuchel provides Kobbie Mainoo injury update after Man Utd star misses England game READ MORE :

Asked if he'd be happy to leave permanently rather than on loan again, Vitek replied: "I am ready for both, to be fair. Depends what the club wants and also depends on the options. We will see.

‌



"There have been a few interests on the table. But we hope to get the best one and hopefully it will happen soon."

Those interested clubs are reportedly Hull City and Ipswich Town, both of whom were promoted to the Premier League last season. "My mind is still the same," Vitek added.

"I want to play. I want to play every week and that is the goal for next season. I think hopefully I will find out soon where that is going to be. I think I grew over the past two-and-a-half years when I went on a few loans. I grew in a person-wise, on the pitch as well."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's numbers do not do justice to his genius - but second World Cup will
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's numbers do not do justice to his genius - but second World Cup will

Gianni Infantino said the tournament would not have been 'an incredible success without Donald Trump' but it is the world's greatest player who has made it truly compelling

View 4 Images Lionel Messi has scored eight goals at World Cup 2026 (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

In theory, it was his wrong foot - as if he has got a wrong foot. Across the edge of England’s six-yard box was a cordon of tall defenders. But he still picked out Lautaro Martinez. In the added minutes of a World Cup semi-final that can scramble the coolest head, he picked out Martinez and invited him to send Argentina to the final.

‌



When all is said and done about England’s capitulation in Atlanta last Wednesday, it was another chapter in the epic, footballing tale being written by Lionel Messi. And should he lead Argentina to back-to-back World Cup triumphs, the only unpalatable sight in New Jersey will be of Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump sharing the stage with the greatest footballer of all time.

‌



Harry Kane's sad admission to England teammates spotted by lip reader after France win READ MORE :

Argentina stars taunted England from team bus after World Cup win as cutting message revealed READ MORE :

Their double act in New York ahead of tonight’s final between Argentina and Spain was nauseous on a predictably grand scale. Sorry, it is no double act. It is puppeteer and puppet. Jonny, as Trump calls him, says what Trump wants him to say.

‌



And on this occasion, Jonny said: “You don’t need people to compliment you, Mr President, but this World Cup would not have been such an incredible success without you.” No, he does need people to compliment him, and Infantino has been happy to oblige. He invented FIFA’S Peace Prize for him, for goodness sake.

Whether or not World Cup 2026 has been ‘an incredible success’ or not is, as usual, a subjective matter. But to be scrupulously fair, even the most sceptical must have enjoyed it to some extent.

The 48-team format did not produce as many mismatches and dead rubbers as we might have thought.

‌



View 4 Images Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino will present the World Cup trophy to the winners in New Jersey (Image: Getty)

It gave us some nice stories, the Cape Verde journey being the standard-bearer for an expanded competition. And there has been some enthralling football in the knockout stages.

Few would complain about having an extra knockout stage. Hands up, I started the World Cup vehemently opposed to a 48-team event … now, a 64-team event would not bother me.

‌



The breadth and gaiety of the competing nations and their supporters have been sights to behold and the venues have, in the main, looked sensational. There is, though, a lengthy snag list, headed by the exorbitant cost of getting into games and being there.

It will go down as the most-attended World Cup but it is still THE rip-off World Cup. And then there was the banning of Somalian referee Omar Artan, the poor treatment of the Iranian national team and the lifting of Folarin Balogun’s suspension after the Trump intervention.

View 4 Images Lautaro Martinez headed Lionel Messi's cross home to end England's hopes of winning the World Cup (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



“Jonny made yet another of his good decisions,” Trump said on Friday. And then there was the hydration-break system, a running sore through the four and a half weeks of competition.

But in the end, FIFA - and Infantino - will get away with fundamentally changing the format of a football match. They will get away with it because the football has been largely compelling.

And nothing has been more compelling than Messi, at the age of 39, redefining his greatness. Here are some stats from this World Cup.

‌



Most shots - 34 (Messi). Most chances created - 25 (Messi). Most take-ons completed - 25 (Messi). Most accurate crosses - 19 (Messi). Most through balls - 15 (Messi). Most goal involvements - 12 (Messi). Most big chances created - 8 (Messi). Most goals - 10 (Mbappe, Messi second with 8).

View 4 Images Lionel Messi inspired Argentina to their World Cup win in Qatar (Image: Getty Images)

They are remarkable numbers but those of us who have watched Messi for over two decades know that numbers do not even come close to doing justice to his genius. Argentina’s antics during and after the semi-final win were not to everyone’s taste. There will be little support for them in England.

‌



But to see Messi inspire his nation was a sight to behold in Qatar in 2022, and is even more so four years later. So, when Infantino tells Trump this World Cup would not have been such an incredible success without him, he is fundamentally wrong.

This World Cup would not have been such an incredible success - if that is what you think it is - without Lionel Messi. And it will be hard to begrudge him a remarkable final act.

Sports.title: BBC's Joe Hart in bizarre video before World Cup final with pundit DRENCHED in monsoon weather
Sports.content:
BBC's Joe Hart in bizarre video before World Cup final with pundit DRENCHED in monsoon weather

Ex-England goalkeeper Joe Hart filmed a bizarre video on Saturday as he was caught up in torrential rain before working on the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina

View Image Joe Hart was caught in a torrential downpour at the World Cup (Image: joehartofficial/Instagram)

Joe Hart lost his shoes and was left drenched after torrential rain hit New York ahead of the World Cup final.

‌



Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Hart took to Instagram after a walk in The Big Apple turned into an underwater scene when pouring rain caused chaos in the United States on Saturday. Hart, who has been a familiar face during BBC's World Cup coverage this summer, has travelled out to the US alongside the likes of Wayne Rooney and Micah Richards to work as a pundit for Sunday's final.

‌



But while he was having a chilled walk, torrential rain caused Hart to get drenched. In a video on his Instagram story, the 39-year-old said: "The weather is absolutely banging here, shoes are off, trainers are ruined, COME ON!"

‌



The downpour forced Hart to walk barefoot as he was pictured with his shoes instead in his hands. As well as that, his white t-shirt was sodden and his sunglasses were nowhere to be seen on his head.

Hart then decided to pan the camera round to show the puddles of rain on the road with a car trying to make its way through the flash flood. Meanwhile, people with umbrellas ran to shelter and tried to get from the rain.

Real reason Argentina President won't attend World Cup final with Donald Trump READ MORE :

It's not the first time Hart has surrounded himself with water in recent days, after he joined ex-Manchester United forward Rooney in rowing the River Hudson in New York. Rooney agreed to row if Norway reached the quarter-final after the Scandinavian nation performed the infamous Viking Row celebration at the World Cup.

‌



Although Rooney initially suggested he would row the River Mersey, he changed to the River Hudson instead upon arriving into New York for the final week of the tournament. And as Norway beat Brazil to progress to the last eight, Rooney kept to his wish as he was captured on the Hudson rowing along with Hart and Richards.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Hart, Richards and Rooney are poised to be part of the BBC punditry team working on Sunday's World Cup final between Spain and Argentina at the MetLife Stadium.

‌



Luis de la Fuente's Spain are hoping to win the tournament for the second time and the first time in 16 years, while Lionel Scaloni's Argentina are hoping to go back-to-back after running out on top four years ago in Qatar.

Spain progressed through to the showpiece final following a 2-0 win against France on Tuesday, while Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 and get to their third final in four tournaments.

Sports.title: Spain star calls out Donald Trump and confirms if he'll shake his hand at World Cup final
Sports.content:
Spain star calls out Donald Trump and confirms if he'll shake his hand at World Cup final

Spain striker Borja Iglesias has confirmed whether he will shake hands with Donald Trump at the 2026 World Cup final, having made his personal feelings towards the US President very clear

View 2 Images Borja Iglesias of Spain has spoken about the prospect of meeting Donald Trump (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

Spain star Borja Iglesias has called out Donald Trump for ‘struggling with fundamental values’ but has vowed to reluctantly shake the US President’s hand. The MetLife Stadium in New Jersey will host the final on Sunday evening, where Spain and Argentina will go head-to-head for the honour of being crowned world champions.

‌



Trump is expected to be in attendance for the match, having not previously attended a single game throughout the tournament so far. The US President is expected to hand over the trophy to the winning team on Sunday night.

‌



Spain won the World Cup in 2010 and are bidding to win the tournament for the second time on Sunday, but Iglesias has opened up on the mixed emotions he’s feeling about the prospect of meeting Trump.

‌



Real reason Argentina President won't attend World Cup final with Donald Trump READ MORE :

"There's a protocol and a commitment to fulfill out of politeness, even though what my gut tells me to do differs from what I should do," he said.

"I like people who fight for progress and for fundamental values to be upheld, and I think Trump struggles with that."

The striker has now provided additional insight into that potential meeting, but admitted he will shake hands with the President.

‌



"I don't want to go to prison,” Iglesias told Spanish press. "I hope to greet him at a time when we are all very happy, and that it passes very quickly and I can forget about it.

"I don't think this is the time to create controversy. People know perfectly well what I think. I would love to do many things, but the reality is that even if people think I am all-powerful, I don't have that much power to tackle certain things."

View 2 Images US President Donald Trump will attend the World Cup final (Image: Saul Loeb/Pool AFP via AP)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Iglesias has been used sparingly at this summer's tournament but has not been afraid to voice his opinion over several on-field issues in recent years.

He has consistently addressed the subject of homophobia and supported pro-Palestine protests. The striker also criticised former Spanish FA boss Luis Rubiales after he was convicted of sexual assault for kissing a player following the Women's World Cup final three years ago.

‌



Iglesias' remarks follow Spanish icon Joan Capdevila publicly appealing to Trump for assistance after being refused a visa to attend the final.

The 2010 World Cup winner suggested he was denied entry after playing in a game in Iran, writing: "I NEED HELP. They just told me that I can't travel to the final with my kids because my ESTA has been denied.

"Can anyone help me with this? You have no idea how excited I was to be there with all my 2010 teammates and this team to cheer them on.

Article continues below

"I can't believe they're not letting me into the USA... and that I'll miss a moment like this with my kids who love soccer so much. If anyone knows how to fix this, I'll be grateful to you for life."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland raises eyebrows as new comments about England World Cup defeat surface
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland raises eyebrows as new comments about England World Cup defeat surface

Norway star Erling Haaland's unusual comments before his team's World Cup exit at the hands of England have come to light

View 2 Images Erling Haaland anticipated Norway's World Cup exit (Image: @erling/Youtube)

Norway and Manchester City striker Erling Haaland has got fans talking after it emerged he expected his national team to lose to England at the World Cup. The 25-year-old scored twice in a round of 16 victory over Brazil but drew a blank when Stale Solbakken's side fell at the quarter-final stage.

‌



England admittedly went into the meeting as favourites, having topped their group. However, Haaland's comments have raised some eyebrows.

‌



"England tomorrow, quarter-finals in the World Cup. I expect England to win and us to go out," the Leeds-born striker said in a YouTube video. "Then we're going to head straight to Norway, Oslo, greet the king. Bit emotional, it's been nice but now it's time to call it a day."

‌



Fans were taken aback by the certainty in the clip. One asked: "What was that? [I] had to listen twice to believe. Why was he so confident in that?"

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

BBC commentator instantly apologises after Danny Murphy outburst in England vs France READ MORE :

Bukayo Saka makes painful England admission and Euro 2028 vow after World Cup star turn READ MORE :

"He didn’t expect to beat Brazil. He was shocked when they did it," wrote a second. A third wondered aloud whether the footage had been faked before being directed to the star's YouTube page.

‌



Others, however, thought it reflected well on him. "Haaland is a player who acknowledges the accomplishments of other teams and players and downplays his own achievements which is what makes him so relatable and likeable," one replied.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Haaland played in five of Norway's six World Cup matches, scoring seven goals. The return leaves him with a remarkable 62 senior international goals in just 55 appearances.

‌



England, however, were the one team able to keep him out. Andreas Schjelderup scored the Scandinavians' goal, only for a Jude Bellingham brace to turn the tie on its head.

View 2 Images Haaland drew a blank against England (Image: Icon Sport via Getty Images)

"We are touched by the fact we have done so well and it's brought people together in Norway," Haaland, who was substituted during extra-time, said after the elimination. "There is a lot of positivity in the joy we have had in our country and here as well.

‌



"It's difficult to think over things right now. It's quite an insane event. You really do have to experience this. That has been my goal.

"I would like to put Norway on the map and establish us as one of the best teams in the world. I think we have sold Norway on the map here."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi drops huge retirement hint ahead of World Cup final - 'The last tango'
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi drops huge retirement hint ahead of World Cup final - 'The last tango'

Lionel Messi will lead Argentina into Sunday's World Cup final against Spain and with just hours until kick-off, the Inter Miami superstar has dropped a hint regarding his future

View Image Lionel Messi could hang up his boots (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Lionel Messi has appeared to call Sunday's World Cup final 'the last tango' in a cryptic social media post. Messi, who turned 39 last month, and his Argentina team-mates will take on Spain in what could prove to the final chapter of his storied career.

‌



Despite recently signing a new contract with Inter Miami which keeps him at the club until 2028, the idea of hanging up his boots after winning another World Cup triumph with Argentina has been floated. Messi has now further fuelled speculation over his potential retirement, either at international level or altogether, with a post on Instagram.

‌



On Saturday night, the forward shared a photo of himself draped in the Argentine flag. Messi added: "What a journey we're having together, @adidasfootball… with 'The Last Tango'… Let's go for the final, let's go Argentina!!!"

‌



'The Last Tango' is notably the name for his signature pair of boots manufactured by Adidas. Later on Saturday, Messi shared a group photo of Argentina's players and staff at their team hotel, and accompanied it with an emotional caption.

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

Flash floods swamp New York causing travel chaos hours before World Cup final READ MORE :

"The best part of all these years wasn't just the titles, but the whole journey," the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner wrote. "Sharing every day with this group, competing together, getting back up in tough times, and enjoying every step.

‌



"Thank you to each of my teammates, the coaching staff, and everyone who works every day to keep this national team a family. Whatever happens tomorrow, this group has already written a story we’ll never forget and that no one can erase. GO ARGENTINA."

Before the tournament, Messi was coy on whether he'd even be involved due to his age. It's safe to assume, then, that he'll already have retired when the next World Cup takes place in 2030, with Argentina co-hosting the tournament for one match.

Should Lionel Messi retire after the World Cup? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Even at 43, though, he'd likely still have the magic to wow fans and destroy opponents. His second-half display against England in the semi-finals was vintage Messi, providing the assists for both goals as Argentina came from behind to reach New Jersey.

It'll be Messi's third World Cup final, having made the 2014 and 2022 editions. Argentina are looking to become the first country to win back-to-back World Cups, matching what rivals Brazil did in 1958 and 1962.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
