It urged Wangchuk to cooperate with doctors "if he so chooses."

The high court directed the Centre, Delhi Police, and Safdarjung Hospital authorities to submit a status report on Wangchuk's condition within three days and listed the matter for hearing on July 24.

Wangchuk was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital on Saturday after Delhi Police removed him from the protest site at Jantar Mantar, citing medical advice and directions of the Delhi high court. He had been on an indefinite hunger strike since June 28, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in national examinations, including the NEET paper leak case.

World.title: Employees welcome extension of OPS benefits
World.content:
Government employees who benefited from the State government’s decision to extend the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) to a section of employees previously covered under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) participated in a thanksgiving meeting at the Swarna Bharathi Indoor Stadium in the city on Sunday, expressing gratitude to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu.

The programme organised under the aegis of the AP DSC Forum, the Noble Teachers’ Association, the PRTU, the APTF and other employees’ and teachers’ associations representing OPS beneficiaries in north Andhra, drew a large number of employees and their family members from the region. Employees poured milk over a portrait of the Chief Minister in a symbolic gesture of gratitude and raised slogans thanking the government for restoring pension benefits.

Government Whip in the Legislative Council Vepada Chiranjeevi Rao, TDP State president and Gajuwaka MLA Palla Srinivasa Rao, Visakhapatnam East MLA Velagapudi Ramakrishna Babu, Visakhapatnam North MLA P. Vishnu Kumar Raju, and Graduates’ constituency MLCs Alapati Raja, Kancharla Srikanth and Perabathula Rajasekhar attended the programme.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Chiranjeevi Rao said the coalition government had provided financial security to nearly 11,000 families by extending the OPS to eligible employees. He said employees retire from service, but their families continue to depend on post-retirement financial support, making pension security an important welfare measure. He alleged that government employees had faced difficulties in receiving dearness allowance arrears and reimbursement of medical bills during the previous government’s tenure.

Mr. Chiranjeevi Rao said that the government had extended OPS, family pension and gratuity benefits to employees recruited under the 2004 notification who entered service later for technical reasons. He also credited the Chief Minister with raising teachers’ salaries on a par with those of revenue employees, and appealed to employees and teachers to work with the government for the State’s development.

Mr. Palla Srinivasa Rao said the coalition government remained committed to the welfare of employees and teachers. Mr. Vishnu Kumar Raju alleged that teachers had been humiliated during the previous government’s tenure by being deployed to regulate queues at liquor outlets. Mr. Velagapudi Ramakrishna Babu said the government would support every measure benefiting employees. Representatives of various employees’ and teachers’ associations also addressed the gathering and thanked the State government for extending the pension benefits.

World.title: Linking FRS attendance with examination fee payment in DIETs approved
World.content:
The State government has accorded permission for linking the attendance data generated through facial recognition system (FRS) with the examination fee payment process and examination eligibility of student-teachers.

The system will be applied to all State-run District Institute of Education and Training (DIETs) and private colleges with Diploma in Elementary Education and Diploma in Pre School Education. The process will be mandated from the current academic year.

The practice, officials said, will help create an integrated system to ensure that only eligible students can register for examinations and make the examination process more efficient and transparent.

World.title: IMA conference in Kozhikode seeks to strengthen general practitioners
World.content:
A medical conference held here on Sunday (July 19, 2026) called for steps to strengthen the role of general physicians in public health to cut down treatment costs.

The conference titled ‘CGPCON 2026’ was organised by the Indian Medical Association’s (IMA) College of General Practitioners, its oldest academic wing headquartered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Around 300 doctors from across South India attended it.

Highlighting a trend among a section of people to either ignore their ailments or to directly approach specialist doctors, the organisers said that this has led to high healthcare expenses. Numerous clinics and small hospitals in the country have closed down too. “Vulnerability and fatality from emerging illnesses are very high among those having various co-morbidities. In a set up where the general practitioner system is at the heart of medical care, incidences of and complications from lifestyle diseases will be very less,” Sankar Mahadevan, organising chairman of the conference, said.

He said that in all developed nations across the world, attending to primary care from general practitioners at first for any ailment was mandatory. Approaching a general practitioner for prompt evaluation and primary care would always ensure better health outcome, he added. The conference also urged the government to post family physicians in every taluk and district hospitals with immediate effect. Establishing a good referral system in healthcare is also the need of the hour, the organisers said.

Around 10 papers on commonly found diseases among the people and the modern treatment methods were presented. It was followed by a panel discussion for family physicians and general practitioners. An emergency training workshop was held for the delegates. Postgraduate medical students also presented their research papers.

The event was inaugurated by IMA national vice-president R. Ramesh. IMA’s national, State, and regional functionaries spoke. Oliver Noone, prominent doctor from Kozhikode, was presented with an award in memory of A. Ramanathan, prominent general practitioner from the city.

World.title: Revanth Reddy says Telangana will produce future Football World Cup stars
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Sunday (July 19) reaffirmed his passion for football and expressed confidence that India would one day qualify for the FIFA World Cup finals, with several players from Telangana forming part of the national team.

In a message shared on social media ahead of the FIFA World Cup final, the Chief Minister described himself as a “die-hard sports and football lover” and recalled the memorable occasion when football legend Lionel Messi visited Hyderabad to interact with children from Telangana.

Mr. Revanth Reddy said bringing Messi to Hyderabad was not merely a symbolic event but reflected a larger vision of promoting football and inspiring young talent in the State.

“I am convinced that one day the Indian football team will play in the FIFA World Cup finals and even host the tournament. Mark my words, several of those future stars will be from Telangana,” he said.

The Chief Minister said his support for the FIFA World Cup stemmed from a long-term commitment to nurturing sporting talent and creating opportunities for young footballers. He expressed hope that Telangana’s youth would emerge as key contributors to India’s rise in international football.

World.title: Faced with outrage, Kerala Health Minister makes a U-turn on DYFI food packet distribution in hospitals
World.content:
Faced with intense civic and political outrage, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan on Sunday flip-flopped on his opposition to the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI)’s free ‘pothichoru’ (food parcel) distribution in over 60 government hospitals in Kerala.

On Saturday, Mr. Muraleedharan had said that the government would put an end to the distribution of food packets on hospital premises under the banner of political parties. He said the government would start community kitchens in hospitals. The statement led to a huge uproar, with the DYFI and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] accusing the Minister of attempting to scuttle a humanitarian initiative that has continued without a break since the DYFI launched it in 2017.

By Sunday evening, the Minister’s office issued a clarification saying that the government is not against free food distribution programme at hospitals. “The Minister’s earlier statement was made regarding the Government Medical College in Alappuzha, where some organisations have encroached upon the hospital’s land in the name of food distribution. It need not be seen as a general statement. The government’s wish is that the poor get food,” said the statement.

DYFI national president A.A. Rahim told The Hindu that governments across the world usually attempt to get the maximum number of community organisations involved in health and social security sectors, but the UDF government has unfortunately taken an opposite view, which is not beneficial to anyone.

“The DYFI organises blood donation in all hospitals and has hundreds of ambulances in which patients in critical condition are taken to hospitals. Would the Minister stop these also? Several organisations, including the Indian Union Muslim League’s C.H. Muhammed Koya Foundation, organise initiatives on hospital premises under their banner. Many voluntary organisations have been distributing food packets even before the DYFI initiative, but what makes our model different is the participation of people of all religions and belonging to various political parties, who prepare the food which is consumed by people from all walks of life,” said Mr. Rahim.

From 2017

The DYFI’s initiative began in 2017 from Vilappilsala in Thiruvananthapuram where the local unit started distributing food to a charity organisation which rescued people from the streets. The organisation’s district committee later implemented it with the brand name ‘Hridayapoorvam’ at the Government Medical College Thiruvananthapuram, with an initial batch of 600 packets. The programme has now expanded to over 60 hospitals, with a total of over 40,000 food packets distributed daily.

According to Mr. Rahim, the DYFI district committees prepare distribution charts for the whole year, with each local unit collecting food packets from homes twice or thrice a year. He accused Mr. Muraleedharan of hypocrisy in naming a public-funded hospital after his father K. Karunakaran, while scuttling a free food distribution programme.

No alternatives: Pinarayi

Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said that the UDF government is giving priority to denying food to the needy without finding solutions to the unprecedented mismanagement in the health sector. “This is an exemplary voluntary work being done for patients and caregivers without political considerations. Only those who are inhumane can mix the poison of narrow politics in it. This distribution of packets, which is being carried out by everyone, beyond party politics and caste and religious differences, is being hastily banned before alternative systems are implemented. What benefit does the government intend to gain by doing so?” asked Mr. Vijayan in a Facebook post.

BJP stance

Significantly, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader K. Surendran also lashed out at the Minister’s stand and said that the government should not view free meal distribution through a political lens. “If all those who received food packets voted for those who gave them, Mr. Muraleedharan would not have been in the Assembly,” he said.

World.title: Woman killed in road accident in K.K. Nagar
World.content:
A 24-year-old woman was killed after being run over by a car in K.K. Nagar on Sunday. The Pondy Bazaar Traffic police have arrested the driver of the car and are investigating.

A senior officer of the city traffic police said the victim Hemalatha, a resident of Sriperumbudur, had come to her brother’s house in Nesapakkam. Hemalatha, her brother and her sister-in-law went to T. Nagar for shopping on two separate two-wheelers.

While proceeding on Anna Main Road towards Ashok Pillar, Hemalatha hit a two-wheeler, which was ahead of her. In the impact both Hemalatha and the other motorist fell on the road. Before Hemalatha could get up, a car ran over her, killing her on the spot. The other motorist escaped with minor injuries.

The Pondy Bazaar Traffic Investigation police, on being alerted, sent Hemalatha’s body to K.K. Nagar ESI Hospital and arrested the car driver Senthil Kumar, 52, who works as a manager in a private bank.

World.title: Telangana government sets up panel to audit private universities as per Supreme Court directions
World.content:
The Telangana government has decided to inspect all private universities in the State in response to directions from the Supreme Court, which has sought detailed information on their establishment, governance, academic standards and regulatory compliance.

The decision is based on the Supreme Court’s directions in the Ayesha Jain vs Union of India case, in which the apex court took note of several complaints relating to private universities, and asked all State governments to conduct comprehensive inspections and submit affidavits covering multiple aspects of their operations.

An official said, in compliance with the order, the government has constituted a high-level committee headed by the Commissioner of Collegiate Education. The committee comprises the Secretary of the Telangana Council of Higher Education (TGCHE) as convenor, the Registrar of JNTU as member-convenor, the Registrar of Palamuru University, the Chief Finance and Accounts Officer of Osmania University and the Assistant Director (Academic-C), Commissionerate of Technical Education, as members.

According to officials, the apex court has directed the States to furnish details on nine key aspects of private universities. These include the rationale behind establishing each university, the objectives of the sponsoring organisation, and whether any feasibility or policy studies were undertaken before their establishment.

The court has also sought information on land allotments or other concessions granted by the State, the governing bodies managing the institutions, and the process followed for appointing their members.

The affidavit of the committee is also expected to explain the admission process, including entrance criteria and whether they comply with statutory provisions, as well as the recruitment of teaching staff and adherence to the University Grants Commission (UGC) norms.

Further, the court has asked States to clarify the mechanism for monitoring compliance with regulations, the frequency of inspections, and the action taken in cases of violations.

A significant focus of the inquiry is on the financial functioning of private universities that claim to operate on a “no-profit, no-loss” basis. Committee will look into whether institutional funds are being diverted for the benefit of promoters or their family members and whether accounts have been audited.

In addition, the committee has to verify whether academic staff are being paid salaries in accordance with statutory minimum wage provisions and UGC norms, and whether salary records have been examined for compliance. Based on the inspection reports, the Telangana government will prepare and submit a detailed affidavit before the Supreme Court.

World.title: 50 spotted deer translocated from Sasan Gir to Mandvi forest to increase prey base, reduce human-wildlife conflict
World.content:
A total of 21 spotted deer were released on May 23, followed by 16 on June 18 and another 13 on June 24, taking the total number to 50.

Aimed at mitigating incidents of human-wildlife conflict, the Gujarat Forest department has translocated 50 spotted deer from the Sasan Gir Wildlife Division to the Mandvi Forest Range in Surat district. The initiative is intended to strengthen the natural prey base for carnivores, enhance biodiversity, and support long-term ecological balance in South Gujarat, an official release said on Sunday.

“The translocation was carried out in three phases between May and June this year. A total of 21 spotted deer were released on May 23, followed by 16 on June 18 and another 13 on June 24, taking the total number to 50,” the release said.

Conservator of Forests (Surat Circle) Puneet Nayyar said that forest officials had carried out detailed habitat assessments to identify sites capable of sustaining the released animals.

World.title: ‘Ronaldo is all-time favourite; don’t mind Spain or Argentina winning’: Sindhu
World.content:
PV Sindhu might be using all the data points on loading, in-game metrics and recovery, but she said she prioritized the very human – simple interaction with her coach, as she returned to title winning ways at the Japan Open. It was a ‘waited and wanted’ title, she said.

“Training can go up and down because one day you train hard. Next day you might feel tired. It’s important to talk to my coach and know why it’s happening and strategise,” said the Super 750 winner in an interaction facilitated by BAI. Sindhu cannily noted that while tech and data was useful, she wouldn’t let hard cold numbers push her into a negative mindset.

Speaking to Indian media after her win, Sindhu noted that the long wait for a title had made her careful and even disbelieving when she was on 21-17, 20-17, a point away. “Even after the challenge, I couldn’t believe I’d won because it was almost after 2 years,” she said of getting on top step of the podium.

For someone known for her unfailing fitness for years early on, even the smallest niggles could turn “irritating,” she noted. “It was a tough journey. Niggles took time. I came back. Got injured again. After injury, you doubt yourself, wonder if you will play at 100% again. It can get emotionally draining and mentally low,” she said.

Yamaguchi, despite 30 faceoffs remains a tricky opponent. “We know each other’s games, we play a lot. But I need to be prepared. The slightest chance you give her, once she starts, she will take many points and find her rhythm.”

Sindhu made sure she was consistent in her attack and made fewest unforced errors. When asked if she was close to beating An Se-young, Sindhu noted, “Last two times, i couldve taken a set. Smallest things matter. Every shot selection matters,” she said.

Her hunger was intact. “Yes this title gives me relief, but there are so many tournaments to win,” the elite athlete who goes up to World No 7, said.



On the 15×3 format, Sindhu said she was cognizant of the fact that even if matches were to get smaller, the intensity of every point would increase. She also added shuttlers now needed an all-round game with half smashes, drops, net and clears not just a smashing attack.

Her return to top tier wins however had been focused inward. So even the twars shed were preceded by self belief where she told herself, “It was not over yet.”

The Japan title will be easy to remember as the FIFA final date. “I’m OK with either Spain or Argentina winning. Both are playing well. My all-time favourite is Cristiano, unfortunately he lost,” Sindhu said.

World.title: Not declaring live-in relationship could land couples in jail under Madhya Pradesh’s UCC
World.content:
The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet on Sunday approved the draft Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill, proposing a common civil law for all residents that bans polygamy, criminalises practices such as triple talaq and provides for potential imprisonment of couples in live-in relationships if they don’t declare their status.

According to the Bill, couples in a live-in relationship will be legally required to file a “declaration of live-in relationship” with the registrar within one month of starting to live together. If a partner is under 21, information about the “start and end of the live-in relationship will be sent to their parents/guardians”. The registrar will also send this record to the local police station.

The penalties proposed in the Bill include three months’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 10,000 for not registering the declaration within a month. Giving false information can attract three months’ imprisonment and a fine of Rs 25,000, and failing to file the declaration even after a registrar’s notice can attract up to 6 months’ imprisonment and a fine of Rs 25,000.

The Bill has provisions to consider children born of a live-in relationship to have full inheritance rights. If the male partner in the relationship deserts the woman, she “can claim maintenance through a competent court just as a legal wife would,” as per the Bill.

Monogamy, divorce

The code makes monogamy the norm across all communities. A person may be married to only one living spouse at a time as per the Bill. The minimum age for marriage is fixed at 21 years for men and 18 years for women. Marriages involving invalid consent and prohibited relationships (unless permitted by custom) are barred.

Oral divorce or decisions by informal panchayats are “declared entirely illegal”. A marriage can now be dissolved only on the clear, statutory grounds specified in law. “Accepting, promoting, or forcing degrading or humiliating conditions such as ‘nikah halala’ for remarriage to the same spouse after divorce will be treated as a punishable criminal offence,” the Bill stated.

Exception

Keeping in mind the sizeable population of Scheduled Tribes, amongst the largest in India, the Bill proposes that the law would not apply to Scheduled Tribes covered under Articles 342 and 366(25) of the Constitution (such as Bhil, Gond, Korku, Baiga, Sahariya and Bharia).



The Bill also seeks to extend protection to children, proposing to ban the word illegitimate and give every child equal legal status. Sons and daughters are given equal rights to inherit property, regardless of marital status. Widows and widowers will also be treated equally in the deceased’s property.

The draft legislation is expected to be introduced in the Madhya Pradesh Assembly during the Monsoon Session beginning Monday.

The move also fulfils one of the BJP’s long-standing ideological commitments and a promise repeatedly made by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav after taking office in December 2023. Yadav had constituted a committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Desai to prepare the draft, describing the UCC as essential for ensuring gender justice, equality before law and women’s empowerment. The committee submitted its report to the government earlier this month, paving the way for the cabinet’s approval.

With reference to the International Organisation for Migration (IOM), consider the following statements:

1. IOM is part of the United Nations system.

2. It was established in 1951.

3. It supports migrants only across the member countries of the IOM.

4. IOM functions under the Constitution of the International Organization for Migration

How many of the statements given above are correct?

(a) Only one

(b) Only two

(c) Only three

(d) All four

Relevance: International organisations, their mandates, year of establishment, and relationship with the UN are recurring UPSC Prelims themes. Aspirants should also compare IOM with agencies such as UNHCR, ILO, and ICRC, focusing on their mandates, legal status, and membership.

Explanation

— The International Organisation for Migration (IOM), founded in 1951, is the premier intergovernmental organization in the field of migration. It is dedicated to the notion that humane and orderly mobility benefits both migrants and society. The IOM is a part of the United Nations system. Hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct.



— IOM assists migrants all over the world in establishing effective solutions to the changing dynamics of migration, and as such, it is a valuable source of advice on migration policy and practice. The IOM operates worldwide, including in non-member states and territories, where governments request help or humanitarian needs arise. Hence, statement 3 is not correct.

— The Organisation is guided by the ideals stated in the United Nations Charter, which include ensuring human rights for all. Respect for migrants’ rights, dignity, and well-being remains vital. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

(Source: http://www.iom.int)

QUESTION 2

Consider the following statements:

1. It is Iran’s only ocean-facing deep-water port.

2. The port is strategically significant for regional trade.

3. The port is situated outside the Strait of Hormuz on the Gulf of Oman.

The above-mentioned statements refer to:

(a) Port of Shahid Rajaee

(b) Bushehr Port

(c) Caspian Port

(d) Chabahar Port

Relevance: UPSC can frame questions on the location of ports, seas, straits, and transport corridors. Aspirants should also map important ports along the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, and the Strait of Hormuz.

Explanation



— The United States launched fresh airstrikes on Iran, hitting the strategic port city of Chabahar for the first time since the war began, as Washington expanded its military campaign beyond the Strait of Hormuz.

— Chabahar is Iran’s only ocean-facing deep-water port and sits outside the Strait of Hormuz on the Gulf of Oman. The port is strategically significant for regional trade.

— The US military officials said strikes in Chabahar were aimed at maritime infrastructure and military facilities that are reportedly believed to be aiding Iran’s ability to threaten commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

QUESTION 3

Consider the following countries:

1. Bangladesh

2. Thailand

3. Vietnam

4. Afghanistan

5. Sri Lanka

6. Maldives

Which of the countries given above are the member countries of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)?

(a) 1, 2, 4 and 5 only

(b) 1, 2 and 5 only

(c) 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6

(d) 1, 2, 5 and 6 only



Relevance: Regional groupings such as BIMSTEC, ASEAN, SAARC, IORA, and SCO are frequently tested in UPSC Prelims. Aspirants should be familiar with their member countries, geographical scope, and differences in membership.

Explanation

— National security chiefs of BIMSTEC countries vowed to jointly combat regional security challenges and endorsed new guiding principles to streamline maritime law enforcement coordination.

— BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) comprises India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan, and all of them have stakes in the developments in the Indian Ocean.

— The meeting held in New Delhi was hosted by National Security Advisor Ajit Doval. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said the national security advisors and heads of delegations discussed practical and result-oriented solutions to combat terrorism and organised crime, and to ensure security in the cyber, maritime and energy domains.

Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.



QUESTION 4

The Falkland Islands were recently in the news. They are located:

(a) Northern Pacific Ocean

(b) Southern Pacific Ocean

(c) Northern Atlantic Ocean

(d) Southern Atlantic Ocean

Relevance: Islands, seas, straits, and disputed territories frequently feature in UPSC Prelims, especially when linked to geopolitical developments. Aspirants should be able to locate important island groups and associate them with the correct ocean, neighbouring countries, and strategic significance.

Explanation

— While celebrating their 2-1 triumph over England in the semi-final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Argentina’s Lautaro Martínez and Giovani Lo Celso held aloft a banner that read: ‘Las Malvinas son Argentinas’. It translates to: ‘The Falkland Islands [Malvinas] are Argentine.’

— The Falkland Islands — or Islas Malvinas, as they are known in Argentina — have remained at the centre of a sovereignty dispute between Argentina and the UK since Britain reasserted control over the islands in 1833.



— The Falkland Islands are an archipelago located in the South Atlantic Ocean.

Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

QUESTION 5

The nuclear site ‘Pickaxe Mountain’ was in the news. The site is located in:

(a) United States

(b) Canada

(c) Israel

(d) Iran

Relevance: International hotspots involving nuclear facilities and strategic military infrastructure are frequently in the news and are important from the perspective of international relations and map-based questions.

Explanation

— US President Donald Trump has threatened to strike Iran’s heavily fortified nuclear facility known as “Pickaxe Mountain”, putting renewed focus on one of Tehran’s most secretive underground sites that experts say is designed to withstand conventional bunker-buster bombs.



— Pickaxe Mountain, also known as Kūh-e Kolang Gaz Lā, is a deeply buried underground nuclear facility under construction near Iran’s main uranium enrichment complex at Natanz.

— It lies about 1.5 km south of the Natanz nuclear facility in central Iran. The site is dug into a mountain in the Zagros range, making it far more protected than Iran’s existing underground facilities.

Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

World.title: ‘I miss making money’: Maria Goretti on choosing motherhood over fame
World.content:
Former VJ and Arshad Warsi’s wife, Maria Goretti, recently opened up about stepping away from fame to be a mother. She also admitted that while she sometimes misses the financial independence and appreciation that came with her work, she has no regrets about choosing motherhood.

The couple got married on Valentine’s Day, February 14, 1999, after dating for 8 years. Speaking about her journey on The Aditi Govitrikar Show, Maria said she often misses the money she earned during her stint as an MTV VJ, but felt fulfilled by the recognition she received at the time.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

Maria Goretti on choosing motherhood

“I miss making money. Let me put that very honestly. It’s like the kind of money I commanded at one point in time. I took a different route… but I also feel that when I worked and when I was an MTV VJ, there was so much appreciation and I got so much that I was actually satiated,” she said.

She recalled consciously choosing to stay home after becoming a mother. “When I had the kids, I wanted to sit. Today, when I am at home and I’m knocking on teenage doors, I sometimes feel: why am I at home for this? But no, the fact of the matter is that I had a great time,” she laughed.



Maria also spoke about discovering a different side of her personality after leaving television. Despite being known as a confident presenter, she realised she struggled to socialise without the structure of her professional role.

“I realised I became very brave when I had a camera next to me, and I was far more friendly and open because I think it came with the job,” she said, adding, “If I have to do an interview, I will make friends with everyone here… But I realised without that I couldn’t make friends and I was actually quite an introvert.”

Arshad Warsi’s tumultuous career

Reflecting on her husband Arshad Warsi’s career, Maria shared that living through both success and difficult professional phases gave the couple a realistic perspective on fame. She recalled how the family’s perception of success would sometimes be reflected in the number of bouquets arriving on the actor’s birthday.



“The gauge was how many flowers were coming in for his birthday. So some years there would be so many that there would be no place in the house, and then there’d be none,” she said.

She also remembered seeing the actor’s struggling days, despite once enjoying immense popularity. “He was really, really popular and he went to the time when he was just not getting the kind of work that he wanted and I kept telling him don’t do stuff that you don’t like to do because that’s gonna really break your heart.”

“Those were really tough years but what I also remember of those years is that it never made him a bitter person. He holds no grudges. I learnt a lot from watching Arshad,” she said.



Having experienced both highs and lows, she reflected on how the couple remains grounded during successful phases. “We have seen the lowest of the lows so when you know that is possible, what are you gloating about!” Maria said.

Self-worth after becoming parents

Dr Rimpa Sarkar, PhD, Sentier Wellness, Mumbai, said Maria’s experience reflects a common psychological transition many parents, especially mothers, go through after stepping away from their careers for caregiving.

“Many parents, particularly mothers, devote years to caregiving during a phase when their children need them the most. During that time, their identity may gradually become centred around being a parent rather than an individual with personal aspirations, interests, or a professional identity,” Dr Rimpa said.

She explained that as children become more independent, parents often begin questioning their sense of self beyond caregiving. “Rebuilding that sense of self by reconnecting with work, hobbies, friendships, or personal goals is a healthy and natural part of this life stage,” she added.
